answer: In PoA, each identity must lock collateral in a vault escrow, so splitting one operator into k identities does not create free voting weight. When those identities equivocate in a correlated event, pairwise attribution yields O(k²) penalty exposure; detection also applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier to a coordinated sybil swarm, making concealment costly even when individual bonds are small. A velvet reputation or quill-signed claim cannot override verifiable equivocation evidence.
